**What**: Add Rule 6 (the fenced '## Test Intent' header with intent_id and catches_regression_where fields, plus a per-language syntax appendix with canonical Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, and bash fixture examples) and Rule 7 (sibling-case rule, one-header-per-function constraint) to plugins/dso/skills/shared/prompts/behavioral-testing-standard.md.
**Why**: This file is the schema that every downstream test-writer surface (sc-3), reviewer dimension (sc-4), and consumer reference (sc-6) builds on. It is the walking skeleton of the epic.
**Scope**:
- IN: Rule 6 text; intent_id field accepting the 94ed stable-slug format or the 'UNTRACKED -- <rationale>' sentinel; catches_regression_where sentence-completion form; per-language fixture appendix (Python docstring fence, JS/TS block-comment fence, bash line-comment fence); Rule 7 sibling-case rule; one-header-per-function constraint; legacy-test exemption.
- OUT: Updates to consumer files (sc-6), test-writer surface prompts (sc-3), reviewer dimensions (sc-4). **What**: Update the three test-generation surfaces -- plugins/dso/agents/red-test-writer.md, plugins/dso/skills/sprint/prompts/task-execution.md, and the fix-bug RED-phase prompt (concrete path under plugins/dso/skills/fix-bug/, resolved during implementation-plan) -- to reference Rule 6 and Rule 7 and instruct the agent to emit the '## Test Intent' header on every new or modified test.
**Why**: Generation-time binding is the mechanism that puts a header on real tests; without it Rule 6 is inert documentation.
**Scope**:
- IN: Rule 6/7 reference plus header-emission instruction in all three surfaces; synthetic verification via a red-test-writer dispatch against a single-AC fixture task confirming the emitted header parses and its intent_id matches the fixture AC identifier.
- OUT: behavioral-testing-standard.md rule text (draft-1); reviewer dimensions (sc-4); the 69e8 negative-examples retrieval block (different epic, different prompt section).","priority":1,"classification":"new","walkingSkeleton":false,"hasWireframe":false,"doneDefinitions":["red-test-writer.md, sprint/prompts/task-execution.md, and the fix-bug RED-phase prompt each reference Rule 6 and Rule 7 and instruct the agent to emit the '## Test Intent' header on every new or modified test ← Satisfies: sc-3","a dispatch of dso:red-test-writer against a single-AC fixture task produces a test file containing a fenced '## Test Intent' block, an intent_id field, and a catches_regression_where field ← Satisfies: sc-3","the intent_id field in the red-test-writer dispatch output exactly matches the fixture AC identifier ← Satisfies: sc-3","the tests written for this story carry valid Rule 6 headers ← Satisfies: sc-3","unit tests written and passing assert that each of the three surfaces references Rule 6 and Rule 7 ← Satisfies: sc-3"],"considerations":["[Coordination] 69e8-af39 SC4 edits the same three prompt files in a different section (negative-examples-lookup block); d566 lands first, then 69e8 adds its retrieval section. **What**: Extend plugins/dso/docs/workflows/prompts/reviewer-delta-test-quality.md (the build source) with a Tier 1 (assertion shape) dimension and a Tier 2 (articulation) dimension, including the REQUIRED predicate-listing scaffold and the anti-sycophancy prime, then regenerate the compiled plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-test-quality.md via build-review-agents.sh. Also assert the explicit descope: pre-commit-test-quality-gate.sh and semgrep-rules/test-anti-patterns.yaml are NOT extended.
**Why**: The reviewer dimensions are the sole enforcement path for Rules 6/7 (review-only, no hooks). They consume the Rule 6 header schema.
**Scope**:
- IN: Tier 1 dimension (flag assertions on internal method names, private state, mock-invocation counts, source-grep patterns; require observable-output assertions); Tier 2 dimension cases (a) missing/malformed header, (b) tautological catches_regression_where, (c) predicate-listing scaffold for claim-vs-assertion disjointness, (d) catches_regression_where would not actually fail the test, (e) duplicate intent_id without orthogonal suffix; anti-sycophancy prime; build-review-agents.sh regeneration of the compiled agent; negative assertion that the two hook/semgrep files remain unextended.
- OUT: The synthetic-diff review validation run (draft-4); rule text in behavioral-testing-standard.md (draft-1).","priority":1,"classification":"new","walkingSkeleton":false,"hasWireframe":false,"doneDefinitions":["reviewer-delta-test-quality.md contains a Tier 1 (assertion shape) dimension that flags assertions targeting internal method names, private state, mock-invocation counts, or source-grep patterns and requires assertions on observable outputs ← Satisfies: sc-4","reviewer-delta-test-quality.md contains a Tier 2 (articulation) dimension covering all five cases a through e, the predicate-listing scaffold, and the anti-sycophancy prime text ← Satisfies: sc-4","running build-review-agents.sh regenerates code-reviewer-test-quality.md so the compiled agent contains the Tier 1 and Tier 2 dimension text ← Satisfies: sc-4","pre-commit-test-quality-gate.sh and semgrep-rules/test-anti-patterns.yaml contain no Rule 6 or Rule 7 enforcement logic, confirming review-only enforcement ← Satisfies: sc-8","unit tests written and passing assert the Tier 1 and Tier 2 dimensions are present in the regenerated compiled agent ← Satisfies: sc-4"],"considerations":["[Correctness] Tier 2(c) predicate-listing scaffold and the anti-sycophancy prime are weak defenses against LLM reviewer sycophancy on fluent headers; this is accepted residual risk per the epic Scenario Analysis.","[Build] The compiled agent must be regenerated from the delta source via build-review-agents.sh; do not hand-edit the compiled code-reviewer-test-quality.md.","[Descope] sc-8 is a negative constraint; the DD asserts absence of enforcement logic in the two named files rather than presence of a feature."],"scopeSplitCandidate":false,"splitRole":null,"splitPairId":null,"blockedBy":["4312-1616-274f-4817"],"satisfiesCriterion":"sc-4;sc-8"},{"id":"ad98-3abc-ebc5-4f66","title":"As a maintainer, I want every '5-rule' / 'Rule 5' / behavioral-testing-standard reference grep-swept and triaged to version-agnostic phrasing, so no consumer pins a stale rule count","description":"## Description
**What**: Run the case-insensitive grep sweep for '5-rule' / 'five rules' / 'Rule 5' / behavioral-testing-standard across plugins/, tests/, and docs/, update the named consumer files, and triage every match into (i) updated to version-agnostic phrasing or extended to reference Rules 6/7, (ii) explicitly descoped with a one-line rationale, or (iii) already version-agnostic. Produce the full final grep output plus a per-match disposition table for the PR description.
**Why**: Adding Rules 6 and 7 makes any hardcoded 'five rules' / 'Rule 5' reference stale; this sweep prevents silent drift across consumers.
**Scope**:
- IN: The grep sweep; updates to the named consumer files; per-match triage disposition table; PR-description grep output.
- OUT: The Rule 6/7 text itself (draft-1); reviewer dimensions (draft-3).","priority":2,"classification":"new","walkingSkeleton":false,"hasWireframe":false,"doneDefinitions":["the grep sweep for '5-rule' / 'five rules' / 'Rule 5' / behavioral-testing-standard across plugins/, tests/, and docs/ returns no match that remains pinned to a stale five-rule count without a recorded disposition ← Satisfies: sc-6","each named consumer file references the standard with version-agnostic phrasing or enumerates Rules 6 and 7, and red-test-evaluator.md rejection criteria require a Rule 6 header on new test output ← Satisfies: sc-6","a per-match disposition table records each grep match against outcome (i), (ii), or (iii) with a one-line rationale for every (ii) descope ← Satisfies: sc-6","the three rule5 test files assert the rule count version-agnostically and pass ← Satisfies: sc-6","unit tests written and passing assert that the named consumer files contain version-agnostic phrasing ← Satisfies: sc-6","When this story is complete, every new or modified test file authored by this story carries a valid Rule 6 '## Test Intent' header, consistent with the dogfood property of sc-7 ← Satisfies: sc-7"],"considerations":["[Coverage] Pattern validation confirmed 100% coverage of the 14 brainstorm-time consumers; this sweep catches any consumer added between brainstorm and implementation.","[PR-artifact] The full final grep output and triage disposition must be embedded in the implementation PR description, not only in commit messages.","[Dogfood] This story authors and modifies the three rule5 test files plus consumer-phrasing unit tests; those files must themselves carry a valid Rule 6 '## Test Intent' header, satisfying the sc-7 dogfood property on this story's own tests."],"scopeSplitCandidate":false,"splitRole":null,"splitPairId":null,"blockedBy":["4312-1616-274f-4817"],"satisfiesCriterion":"sc-6;sc-7"},{"id":"7e6c-2bad-f302-431d","title":"As a maintainer, I want a synthetic 3-case review fixture proving the test-quality dimensions fire on planted violations and stay silent on legacy blocks, so reviewer precision is demonstrated","description":"## Description
**What**: Build a synthetic diff fixture with three planted violations -- (a) a new test with no header, (b) a new test asserting only on mock.called_with(...), (c) a new test whose intent_id claims a slug but whose only assertion is `assert True == True` -- alongside an unmodified legacy test block, run /dso:review against it, and assert the resulting reviewer-findings.json contains Tier 1 or Tier 2 findings located inside cases (a)(b)(c) and zero such findings inside the unmodified legacy block.
**Why**: Validates that the SC4 dimensions have both recall (fire on real violations) and precision (do not fire on exempt legacy code), closing the loop on the enforcement path.
**Scope**:
- IN: The synthetic fixture diff; the /dso:review run; assertion on findings[] dimension and source_path:source_line placement for the three violations and the legacy block.
- OUT: The reviewer dimension definitions (draft-3); rule text (draft-1).","priority":2,"classification":"new","walkingSkeleton":false,"hasWireframe":false,"doneDefinitions":["a /dso:review run against the synthetic 3-case diff produces a reviewer-findings.json containing at least one Tier 1 or Tier 2 finding whose source_path:source_line falls inside violation (a) ← Satisfies: sc-5","the same reviewer-findings.json contains at least one Tier 1 or Tier 2 finding inside violation (b) and at least one inside violation (c) ← Satisfies: sc-5","the same reviewer-findings.json contains zero Tier 1 or Tier 2 findings whose source_line falls inside any unmodified legacy test block in the diff ← Satisfies: sc-5","the tests written for this story carry valid Rule 6 headers ← Satisfies: sc-5","unit tests written and passing assert the fixture-review output placement of findings across the three violations and the legacy block ← Satisfies: sc-5"],"considerations":["[Observability] The claim-vs-assertion contradiction check (case c) degrades semantically until the 94ed-f55c manifest ships; the fixture should use a slug-format intent_id consistent with the published manifest schema."],"scopeSplitCandidate":false,"splitRole":null,"splitPairId":null,"blockedBy":["1be0-0959-69ff-4ccd"],"satisfiesCriterion":"sc-5"}],"storyDashboard":{"totalStories":5,"uiStories":0,"criticalPath":["4312-1616-274f-4817","1be0-0959-69ff-4ccd","7e6c-2bad-f302-431d"]}}
